weeks.label: Week of Dec 8, 2025
weeks.summary: This week’s release adds team credit auto-refill, stronger team invite/enrollment controls, more reliable file uploads, better study management, and a set of UI/UX improvements across forms and evaluations.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Team credit auto-refill: teams can enable automatic credit refills (including a zero-amount option) with improved form/button behavior and backend support to manage auto-refill operations.

Invites & enrollment improvements: invite members to specific teams, see helpful tooltips and improved member search/list UI, support pending invites and domain-based auto-enrollment, auto-attach OTP signups to a personal team, and update member roles from the UI.

More reliable and higher-capacity uploads: increased maximum concurrent uploads to 5, added concurrency limiting, extended presigned URL expiry to 5 minutes and raised server body limits, plus retry logic, offline detection and connectivity error notifications for robust file uploads.

Study management enhancements: add/remove stars on studies (new backend model and UI integrations), view starred state across study/persona/walkthrough pages, and use new sorting and filtering (type/owner) in the Studies view to find work faster.

Forms and evaluation UX refinements: long-flow warning alerts for studies that exceed screen thresholds, clearer cognitive/heuristic evaluation prompts, and improved alert/layout/connection error handling in submission forms.

weeks.label: Week of Dec 1, 2025
weeks.summary: This week’s release focuses on a major Studies list overhaul, Figma integration, new demo/contact flows and site-wide design updates, plus improved sign-in and session handling.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Revamped Studies view: replaced individual StudyCard views with a unified StudiesView that adds search (with fuzzy matching), sorting, page-size selection with persistence, loading skeletons to avoid flash, and improved mobile sidebar behavior. Column labels were clarified to show Owner and Updated and last-modified user information is now displayed.

Figma integration: add a connection button, OAuth flow, and an Add to Figma dialog so you can post comments and prototypes directly from the app. The Figma feature flag was removed (now enabled by default) and the integration includes improved error handling for API rate limits (some actions will be temporarily disabled when rate limits occur).

New demo and contact flows: public demo request and contact pages with accessible forms and server-side handlers for submissions, updated demo request styling and copy, and a Global Footer integrated across pages.

Homepage and pricing refresh: redesigned home and pricing pages with a new hero, CTA, Capabilities, Data Safety and Trusted By sections, updated pricing cards and FAQ content, and various layout and visual improvements for clarity and engagement.

Sign-in and session improvements: updated sign-in UI (including enhanced Google sign-in), login links standardized to /signin, a session-validation hook was added to require authentication in server actions, and JWT/error logging was hardened for better traceability.

weeks.label: Week of Nov 24, 2025
weeks.summary: This week’s release improves billing and credits, refines AI evaluation results, upgrades file uploads (including Figma metadata), strengthens persona/study safety and UX, and addresses several UI and reliability issues.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Revamped credits and purchasing: added Stripe checkout and webhook handling, a credit ledger and recent-purchases UI, transfer-credits and purchase flows, permission checks and access control for the credits page, and contextual NoCredits/ClaimCompany alerts to guide users to purchase options.

Improved AI evaluation quality: added deduplication utilities and goal-aware filtering, and expanded heuristic evaluation to include context from adjacent screens so reported issues and recommendations are more relevant and less repetitive.

Better file upload and prototype support: added Figma metadata handling and corresponding database updates, improved blob/image handling in the file UI (native img + object URL management), and reset file inputs so users can re-select the same file easily.

Safer persona & study management with clearer UX: prevented accidental persona deletion when in use, added detailed disabled reasons and tooltips in persona/study menus, and implemented cleanup for orphaned studies with clearer failure notifications.

UI and reliability fixes: resolved mobile visibility for heuristic indicators, optimized resize handling to reduce unnecessary updates, added timeout-aware fetch helpers for better API error handling, and polished credit display/formatting and related form behaviors.

weeks.label: Week of Nov 17, 2025
weeks.summary: This week’s release improves team and membership workflows, tightens permissions and persona handling, adds a Credits settings page and clearer account deletion controls, and ships several UI and data fixes (including optional ratings and image/gallery improvements).

sections.title: Highlights
items: Revamped team and company member management: admins can add, remove, activate, deactivate and (GDPR) erase users from the UI; personal teams are preserved where appropriate; memberships now respect active status for access checks; team admins can manage team studies; auto-enrollment, default auto-join teams and related join-policy behavior are implemented, and users are notified / auto-added when reactivated.

Persona and permission improvements: persona creation permissions are now configurable, company personas are shown in persona selectors across evaluation forms, default-team persona handling was added (including presigned URL access for default team resources) and UI components now expose default-team state for consistent behavior.

Credits and account deletion UX: added a Credits settings page and refreshed credits display/actions; introduced a clear danger zone for personal account deletion and improved company deletion flows to remove associated users, continue if S3 cleanup errors occur, and surface clearer messaging.

Ratings and recommendation fixes: ratings are now optional on heuristic/cognitive results and recommendations, and duplicate-rating validation that blocked updates has been fixed to allow valid updates to succeed.

Media and UI refinements: Gallery and evaluation pages were refactored to use an optimized Image component with dynamic dimensions and constraints, improving layout and performance; assorted styling and accessibility tweaks were applied across metadata, avatars and dropdowns.

weeks.label: Week of Nov 10, 2025
weeks.summary: This week brought improvements to team join workflows, a new team switching UI with URL sync, and adjustments to study listings and limits.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Revamped team join request workflow: users can add request notes and admins can record rejection reasons, the join-request UI surfaces these fields, admins are notified when requests arrive, and emails are sent when requests are processed.

Team switching UX: added a TeamSwitcher and updated the studies page so you can change the active team in-app; the selected team is synchronized with the URL so links/bookmarks preserve the chosen team.
Study listings and limits: filtering now includes pending PERSONA studies that have no records so they appear in lists/filters, and study upload limit names were clarified.

weeks.label: Week of Nov 3, 2025
weeks.summary: This week’s release adds configurable team join policies and team-management features, introduces severity ratings for usability issues, and improves heuristic-evaluation reliability and retry behavior. Several UI and error-handling polish changes were also shipped for a smoother experience.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Configurable team join policies and improved team management — browse teams, join (self-join or request), handle join requests in-app, and edit team names and descriptions; supports invite-only/secret team options.

Severity ratings for usability issues — new SeverityBadge UI and full severity handling across cognitive walkthroughs and heuristic evaluation results; severity is stored in the database (with a default “None” option) and can be updated from issue cards.

More reliable heuristic evaluations and retries — improved error handling and status updates for failed studies, automatic deletion of prior heuristic results on re-runs, payload-size logging, presigned-URL handling, model update for evaluations, and a retry-study script to re-run and recover failed studies.

UI and error-handling polish — sidebar now filters menu items by company membership, title consistency fixes ("Teams"), clearer Figma file fetch error messages, and fixes to join-request fetching to ensure accurate updates.

weeks.label: Week of Oct 27, 2025
weeks.summary: This week we shipped persona versioning with UI and API support, improved navigation in company tables, and adjusted authentication timing. Small permission and usability fixes were included.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Persona versioning: implemented database schema and migration, API endpoints, and UI components to create, view, and manage persona versions. Study cards and persona pages now display version information and a related-studies view shows studies across persona versions. Editing permission logic for persona owners was also corrected so owners can always edit.
Pagination and navigation improvements: added pagination controls and navigation icons to company teams and company members tables to improve browsing large lists and overall usability.
OTP expiration updated: one-time passcodes (OTP) expiry is now set to one hour to balance security and user convenience.

weeks.label: Week of Oct 20, 2025
weeks.summary: This week’s release expands persona editing with a complete update flow, new profile fields and a tools section, plus several form usability improvements and better server-side logging for diagnostics.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Full persona update flow: users can edit and save personas via the UI and backend with server-side validation and image handling (upload/generation) to ensure updates persist correctly.

New persona profile fields: employment status and annual recurring revenue (ARR) are now captured in the persona schema and form, and selecting "No influence" for decision power clears budget range inputs automatically.
Tools input and expertise: a new Tools section lets you add multiple tool items for a persona; each tool now supports an expertise field and improved state handling in the form.

Form usability and clarity improvements: channel and industry option ordering was reorganized, job title/employment fields were refined, and image prompt descriptions were clarified to produce more relevant persona images.
Improved server logging and error reporting: CloudWatch logging import and error structure were refined (with pino added to the shared workspace) to provide clearer diagnostics for backend issues.

weeks.label: Week of Oct 13, 2025
weeks.summary: This week we shipped a major set of improvements to the Heuristics Library: new pages and APIs for browsing and managing heuristic families, a streamlined heuristic-set creation experience, and several reliability and evaluation enhancements for AI-powered checks.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Heuristics Library & family management: a new Library page and backend APIs let you browse heuristic families with a refreshed grid/card layout, view family details, and access both shared and company-specific heuristics.

Create and manage heuristic sets: added a full New Heuristic Set flow including a drag-and-drop form, improved validation (react-hook-form), add/remove controls, an Add Example dialog, and creator tracking so heuristics are attributed to the creating user/company.

Improved heuristic evaluation and persona handling: evaluation output now includes label, description and examples; evaluation enforces company access (companyId); persona generation and evaluation code include better error handling and logging; example-violation messaging now has clearer text and a fallback when no examples are available.

Miscellaneous user-facing fixes: removed the optional description field from the Heuristic model, updated the app logo, and improved team-switching behavior (studies page revalidation and nav refresh to clear caches).

weeks.label: Week of Oct 6, 2025
weeks.summary: This week we shipped custom heuristics support and a set of user-facing improvements around heuristic selection, data freshness, and team-aware assets. Several schema and migration tools were added to safely move heuristic and study data to the new model.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Custom heuristics: you can now create and manage custom heuristics. The system persists custom definitions and integrates them into evaluation workflows so teams can use organization-specific heuristics during study review.

Heuristic selection & evaluation improvements: the UI now includes a heuristic selector and the evaluation form updates immediately when a different heuristic or heuristic family is chosen. Backend retrieval and display were updated to respect heuristic families and show the correct heuristic metadata during evaluations.

Schema changes and migration tools: underlying data models were migrated to use heuristicFamilyId and related schema updates. We included migration scripts for heuristics and user credits, plus a utility to migrate studies between teams (including associated S3 files) to help admins transition existing data to the new model.
Team-aware persona images: persona image generation was updated to use teamId rather than userId so generated persona assets are scoped to teams and remain consistent when content is team-owned.
Data freshness after team changes: data fetching now forces fresh user and studies data and revalidates paths after switching teams, so the UI reflects team and membership changes immediately.

weeks.label: Week of Sep 29, 2025
weeks.summary: This week we migrated the AI evaluation worker to the OpenAI Responses API and tuned evaluation prompts for clearer, more actionable feedback; small UI spacing and model-default fixes were also shipped.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Migrated the AI worker to the OpenAI Responses API and updated default model versions; removed unnecessary max-token overrides so evaluation responses use the newer responses flow and updated model defaults for more consistent output.

Refined cognitive walkthrough and heuristic evaluation prompts to produce higher-quality, actionable feedback: evaluations now require explicit references to concrete UI/UX elements, prioritize target-user goals, provide concrete recommendations, and handle missing target-user details more gracefully.
Fixed spacing in Separator components to improve layout consistency in the Next.js app.

weeks.label: Week of Sep 22, 2025
weeks.summary: This week’s release improves exports and file metadata, speeds and stabilizes automated evaluations, refreshes the evaluation upload UI, and adds several team, membership, and study/browsing improvements across the app.

sections.title: Highlights
items: CSV exports and file metadata now preserve original filenames — files include a new originalName field and export formatting/filename handling has been improved so downloads match uploaded names.

Heuristic evaluation and cognitive walkthrough processing upgraded: evaluations can run in batched mode, OpenAI model and token limits are configurable via environment variables, API calls include retry logic and configurable attempt limits, and schemas now record user attribution; logging has been clarified by renaming max_tokens to max_completion_tokens.

Evaluation upload UI redesigned: a new asset carousel with improved fades and sorting, remove buttons on file cards, disabled uploads while lists load, delayed validation until user interaction, clearer form guidance, surfaced upload-limit errors, and stricter personal-team upload limits (with increased overall evaluation image limits where applicable).

Team and membership management improvements: membership status is tracked separately from user status, teams can be renamed inline (table and settings), studies/charges now respect the currently selected team (including showing team credits and redirecting after team switch).

Persona and study browsing enhancements: related-studies carousel added to persona pages, study cards refactored with fixed links and improved layout, and persona image handling adjusted for more reliable display.

weeks.label: Week of Sep 15, 2025
weeks.summary: This week we shipped major team-management improvements and a complete passwordless sign-in flow with rate limiting, plus several UI and reliability fixes.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Enhanced team management: added a team selector in the navigation and sidebar, enabled inviting company members to teams (team admins can invite), added member search/filters and null states, surfaced company team member details, and send invitation emails to newly added members. Visibility and settings were tightened so users see teams they administer.

Passwordless sign-in improvements: implemented OTP and email-link authentication with rate limiting and cooldown handling, improved resend-sign-in UX (formatted cooldown timers, clearer errors, and input handling), updated email templates, and added a HEAD handler to avoid token consumption by email scanners. Session token handling was also improved for consistency and security.

Polish and bug fixes: fixed nav/team popover widths and alignment, kept team creation toast visible, corrected copy in sign-in flows, escaped host variables in OTP emails, and improved OTP error handling and message clearing on input changes.

weeks.label: Week of Sep 8, 2025
weeks.summary: This week focused on company and team management: admins can create and invite members to teams, company membership management was improved with search/sort and role-aware UI, a new company/domain claim and approval workflow was added (with email notifications), and sign-in/enrollment behavior and logging were enhanced.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Company teams: company admins can create teams from the settings, invite company members during team creation, refine member selection in the creation dialog, and toggle visibility of personal teams in the teams view.

Company members management: members list is now searchable and sortable, members can be displayed and updated from the settings, membership roles are surfaced in NavUser and the sidebar, and access to the company page is enforced based on role; invite email wording and dialog spacing were also improved.

Company/domain claim & approval workflow: added a claim dialog with domain association, pending state and authorization checks, plus an approval workflow for company and domain creation that tracks requesters, shows status messages in settings, and sends email notifications for claims.

Sign-in & enrollment improvements: sign-in now logs successes, failures, and first-time sign-ins; enrollment can automatically attach personal teams to companies by email domain; CompanyJoin UX was clarified (including a new checkbox component) to improve the join/claim experience.

weeks.label: Week of Sep 1, 2025
weeks.summary: This week’s release adds organization and company management, moves credits to teams with updated credit handling, improves PDF export/print for heuristic evaluations, and refines the user navigation menu.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Organization & company management: new organization settings and account pages let you view and update company information (including logo and name), manage members and invites, and create or link a company automatically from a user's email domain. Corresponding API endpoints and database models were added to support these flows.

Team-level credits: credits are now owned and consumed at the team level. We added team credits and a CreditLedger, migrated user credits into personal teams, provided migration scripts (including S3 key prefix migration), and updated APIs and UI forms (FormSubmitWithCredits) so studies consume selected team balances.

PDF export & print improvements: added PDF export for heuristic evaluations and refined the print layout (layout tweaks restricted to print mode) to produce cleaner printed/exported reports for heuristics, issues, and info cards.

Navigation & account updates: the user navigation was enhanced to show organization visibility and new menu items, and the account link now reads “Account Settings” for clearer access to account and organization controls.

weeks.label: Week of Aug 25, 2025
weeks.summary: This week we shipped team and ownership support, expanded and improved persona authoring, several UI/UX and study flow fixes, and a simplification of result violation data.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Personal teams and explicit study ownership: new accounts now get a personal team and users have a selectedTeam. Studies now record createdByUserId and require a teamId, and a backfill was run to migrate existing studies to personal teams so team context and ownership are preserved.

Persona form and persona data improvements: added job title and ethnicity fields, increased persona description limit to 500 characters, updated demographic icons, added a helper to disable submit for empty/meaningless values, prevented accidental Enter-submit when Google Places suggestions are visible, and keep study name in sync when a persona name is provided.

UI and study-flow polish: study completion now triggers a route refresh, polling effects correctly include router dependencies, loading uses a Skeleton placeholder on the studies page, Avatar sizing and several button opacities were corrected for better visual consistency.
Result/violation simplification: the violated field has been standardized to a boolean across the schema, interfaces, and database functions, simplifying violation checks and related logic.

weeks.label: Week of Aug 18, 2025
weeks.summary: This week we shipped full persona support (backend, API and UI), added persona selection to studies, improved persona pages with images and demographics, and rolled up several UI and consistency fixes across persona and study screens.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Persona backend and API: added persona processing, storage, database schema updates and new endpoints so personas can be created, stored and retrieved by the app and workers.

Persona page and media: implemented a full persona detail page with session-aware data fetching, profile photo and cover image retrieval (with error handling), a demographics section, and a More menu for extra actions.

Persona selection in studies: added persona selection and optional persona association to cognitive walkthroughs and heuristic evaluations, improved inline persona selector behavior (focus and input handling), and linked evaluation/walkthrough pages to persona detail views.

UI and consistency improvements: normalized heuristic values and fixed label typos, clarified budget range options, improved list editor text wrapping and item styling, and adjusted icon/layout/styling for consistent appearance across persona and study pages.

weeks.label: Week of Aug 11, 2025
weeks.summary: This week delivers end-to-end persona support (DB, AI generation, and UI), a major job-envelope v2 migration with validation and compatibility, new UI components, and several polish fixes across study workflows and exports.

sections.title: Highlights
items: End-to-end Persona support: added a Persona model with relationships to Study and File, backend createPersona handling, study payload/schema updates for persona jobs, and AI-worker support for persona generation (text and image) including image processing and improved error handling.

Persona creation UI and components: new Persona creation page and a reworked PersonaForm (accordion layout, optional name/description/images, goals and list editors, better file handling to avoid overwrites on cancel, and purchaseTriggers accepting string or array). Also added new Command and Popover UI components used by the app.

Job envelope v2 and job-processing overhaul: migrated to a normalized v2 job envelope with a discriminated 'type' field, improved schema validation and parsing, added backward compatibility for legacy job structures, and provided a migration script to normalize existing Study.jobData; enhanced error handling in cognitive walkthrough and heuristic evaluation endpoints and simplified retry/polling logic.

Polish and bug fixes: preserved step values in CSV export, cleaned up polling UI and retry button formatting/behavior, removed unnecessary logs, and minor PersonaForm cleanups for improved readability and UX.

weeks.label: Week of Aug 4, 2025
weeks.summary: This week’s release adds user-facing profile and communication-management features, completes study initialization/finalization with S3 file support and migration tooling, and delivers broad UI and accessibility improvements including an upgrade to Tailwind v4.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Account page & profile management: new Account page and AccountInformation UI let users update their name (with validation and error handling), upload and remove profile images (client + server validation), and see an avatar in the sidebar. Edit controls were polished for accessibility and to avoid layout shifts.

Communication preferences: users can now view and edit notification settings with save/cancel controls. Backend work adds a CommunicationPreferences model, API endpoints to get and update preferences, an event to create defaults for new users, and a backfill script to create defaults for existing users.

Study workflows & file storage: implemented study initialization and finalization flows that upload files to S3 and persist metadata to the database, added corresponding API endpoints, and included a migration script to restructure S3 file keys and update the database to match the new layout.

UI, styling and accessibility improvements: upgraded the app to Tailwind v4 and updated global styles/components (spacing, labels, breadcrumbs), fixed layout overflow and persistent spacing to prevent visual shifts, and improved button/cursor accessibility across account and navigation components.

weeks.label: Week of Jul 28, 2025
weeks.summary: This week’s release adds centralized client-side logging and a logging API, improves error handling and user-facing error pages, moves core study/evaluation DB work to a db-worker service, and ships UI and form improvements including styling, menu upgrades, and upload limits.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Centralized client-side logging and server endpoint — added a client logging utility and a dedicated /api/log endpoint, and integrated logging across authentication, credit requests, and other core flows to improve observability and error tracking.

Improved error handling and user-facing error pages — introduced and refined GlobalError and NotFound components and added custom error pages for both authenticated and public routes for clearer user feedback when issues occur.

Moved database operations to db-worker service — new db-worker controllers and API routes now handle study updates and cognitive/heuristic evaluations; the app calls these endpoints instead of directly using Prisma, centralizing DB logic.

UI and form enhancements — added a Tailwind configuration for styling and animations, upgraded the MoreMenu with surface-based menu items, enforced maximum file upload limits for evaluation forms, and improved file-state synchronization in forms.

Tighter error logging and sign-in/study flow fixes — improved error logging and handling across cognitive walkthrough and heuristic evaluation actions, fixed sign-in redirect behavior, and made study name update/save error handling more robust.

weeks.label: Week of Jul 21, 2025
weeks.summary: This week focused on observability and stability: logging was centralized and improved across services (including CloudWatch support), user session checks and error handling were tightened in the Next.js app, and runtime/worker behaviors were adjusted for clearer production operation.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Centralized and improved logging across services — pino-based structured logs now include a static service field and normalized level casing, CloudWatch integration added in the Next.js app, and CloudWatch emission is gated to production-only environments.

Tighter session validation and clearer error handling in the Next.js app — studies, walkthrough, and evaluation pages now perform explicit session checks and produce improved logs and diagnostics for authentication and data retrieval failures.

Improved worker observability and runtime behavior — extensive logging added throughout db-worker (and additional logging in ai-worker), health-metrics logging interval increased (from 5 minutes to 1 hour), and build/runtime handling for NODE_ENV was adjusted to allow runtime detection.

weeks.label: Week of Jul 14, 2025
weeks.summary: This week we shipped cross-service observability, major form and UI improvements for evaluations and walkthroughs, first-class per-user data in jobs and submissions, and new legal & navigation pages. Changes include better error handling and user-facing feedback for imports and workflows.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Structured logging and observability: added pino-based structured logs and CloudWatch integration across background workers with health metrics and robust error/permission handling; logging initialization is hardened to avoid duplicate setup and noisy fatal logs for missing env or queue errors.

Evaluation and Walkthrough UI upgrades: added Figma prototype import to the Evaluation form, improved import error handling and file validation feedback, added an “additional information” text input, introduced collapsible sections for walkthrough steps (Radix Collapsible), a small Gallery component, and multiple layout/styling refinements for images and dialogs to improve readability.

Per-user data and validation: added a user field to the database schema, job interfaces, and form schemas; form submissions now include user data and AI worker outputs include target-user and additional-context information to make results user-specific.

Content and navigation updates: published Terms and Privacy pages, updated breadcrumbs and links, standardized page names to “Evaluation” and “Walkthrough,” and removed obsolete heuristic pages for clearer navigation.

weeks.label: Week of Jul 7, 2025
weeks.summary: This week we shipped a major update to the Cognitive Walkthrough experience (new client, results UI, and full issue/recommendation workflows), added study attempt tracking plus retry/credit-refund behavior, and fixed authentication and several UI issues.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Cognitive Walkthrough: added a new client and header, redesigned step and results pages, and enabled full issue and recommendation workflows (create, save, delete). Results now support issue filtering and display total steps; walkthrough details accept learnability, usability and discoverability issue types.

Study attempts & retry handling: introduced an attempts field on Study, a postStudyAttempts endpoint and DB update handler to increment attempts, and integrated updateAttempts into the retry flow. Added an optional retry flag on job data and adjusted credit-refund logic so retries and refunds are handled correctly.
Authentication: fixed Google sign-in and removed the legacy AuthError error page handling to streamline sign-in/error behavior.

UI polish and layout fixes: improved InfoCard layout and className handling (padding, source placement), refined CognitiveWalkthrough step/header styling, hidden create-issue button on mobile, and adjusted spacing in accordion/badge components for better readability.

weeks.label: Week of Jun 9, 2025
weeks.summary: This week introduces a new Pricing page with an integrated credit-request flow, improved email notifications for credit purchases, and visual polishing across the app for more consistent presentation.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Added a public Pricing page that displays tiers in a table-based layout and includes an integrated credit-request form for purchasing credits.
Launched styled, branded email templates for credit purchase requests along with automated confirmation emails and clearer message copy for request workflows.

Improved visual consistency across the site by refactoring global styles (margins/padding), enhancing the GlobalHeader with theme-aware styling, and cleaning up the Home layout structure for better stability and readability.
Consolidated backend handling for credit requests by removing the legacy credit-request API route and cleaning up unused imports; request handling is now routed through the new action/email flow.

weeks.label: Week of Jun 2, 2025
weeks.summary: This week we enhanced exports to include more identifying and classification fields, and polished the heuristic accordion UI for clearer labels and badges.

sections.title: Highlights
items: CSV and Excel exports now include heuristic ID, issue ID, recommendation ID, as well as heuristic category and label so exported reports contain full identifiers and classifications.
Heuristic accordion labels now render more clearly and consistently, improving readability and handling of edge cases.
Badge styling in the heuristic accordion has been refined for better contrast and alignment, making status indicators easier to scan.

weeks.label: Week of May 26, 2025
weeks.summary: This week we shipped downloadable exports, improved live study status updates, extended the Heuristic model with new fields, and rolled out several UI and mobile fixes for heuristics management.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Export heuristics and study data as CSV or Excel directly from the More menu — new download options and export logic let you quickly export current data for analysis or sharing.
Live study status polling added so study status updates refresh automatically; polling runs every 15 seconds to balance responsiveness and load.
Heuristic model extended with new category and label fields in the schema, enabling richer categorization and metadata for heuristics.

UI and mobile improvements for heuristics: HeuristicAccordion is now responsive on mobile, the separator before the add-issue button was removed, HeuristicHeader layout/styling were refined, and a JSX bug was fixed for more stable rendering.

weeks.label: Week of May 19, 2025
weeks.summary: This week we shipped major improvements to the heuristic evaluation workflow, updated authentication with Resend email and Google sign‑in, added database timestamping and API support for recommendations, and applied several UX and accessibility fixes.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Revamped heuristic-evaluation flow: new createHEResult endpoint and backend support for creating HE and CW recommendations, plus a large refactor of the HeuristicResults UI to support adding/editing/deleting recommendations and issues (including image selection and dialogs), improved sorting and rendering by step/createdAt, and better mobile/responsive behavior.

Passwordless and social sign-in updates: integrated Resend as a NextAuth provider with a custom email verification template (HTML + text fallback), added a ResendSignIn component with enhanced email validation and error handling, and introduced a GoogleSignIn component — replacing the previous SignIn flow.

Data model and API improvements: added createdAt and updatedAt fields (with @updatedAt automatic timestamps) to CWIssue, CWRecommendation, HEResult and HERecommendation in the Prisma schema, and updated database services and API routes to support recommendation creation and reliable timestamped records.

UX and accessibility fixes: corrected heading levels and margins, improved email-sent confirmation styling and error messages, reduced issue font size, removed textarea resizing, and clarified dialog labels and InfoCard success/error messaging for a cleaner, more consistent experience.

weeks.label: Week of May 12, 2025
weeks.summary: This week focused on improving the heuristic-evaluation experience, extending backend support for walkthroughs/evaluations, adding site-wide notifications, and hardening worker error handling and logging.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Revamped the heuristic evaluation UI: new accordion-based layout, filtering switch, and InfoCard-driven display for issues and recommendations; added inline editing (textarea), improved image handling and layout, and clearer violated-count/state management for deleted items.

Backend and schema enhancements for studies: added update and delete endpoints for cognitive walkthroughs and heuristic evaluations, introduced an AI_HUMAN source type, and started returning step/stepIndex information in evaluation responses.
Added site-wide toast notifications by integrating the sonner Toaster into both authenticated and unauthenticated layouts so users receive consistent feedback across the app.
Improved reliability of background processing: better error handling and success/error logging in AI worker flows and queue job processing to reduce silent failures and surface issues more clearly.

weeks.label: Week of May 5, 2025
weeks.summary: This week focused on improving stability of the AI worker's heuristic evaluations and increasing server request payload limits. These changes reduce flaky evaluations and prevent request rejections for larger payloads.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Added retry logic to heuristic evaluation so transient failures are automatically reattempted, improving overall evaluation reliability.
Introduced a short delay before processing files in heuristic evaluation to reduce race conditions and processing flakiness.
Increased request body size limits for JSON and URL-encoded form data so larger payloads are accepted and fewer requests are rejected.

weeks.label: Week of Apr 21, 2025
weeks.summary: This week we added file-level tracking for heuristic evaluation results, a new file-retrieval API, and refactored AI worker flows to fetch and handle files consistently from the database.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Heuristic evaluation results now include fileId for precise file-level tracking; database schema and ResultData interfaces updated so HE results are related to File records.
Implemented a getFiles endpoint and database service to retrieve files by studyId (query/body/params), enabling other services to fetch study files from the DB.

AI worker processes (heuristicEvaluation and cognitiveWalkthrough) were refactored to fetch files from the database and to use a shared File interface and utility functions for consistent file handling.
Database write paths updated so heuristic evaluation posts connect results to files using fileId, improving result-to-file linkage and traceability.

weeks.label: Week of Apr 14, 2025
weeks.summary: This week we refined the evaluation prompts used by the AI worker—improving clarity, structure, and guidance for both cognitive walkthroughs and heuristic evaluations so outputs are more consistent and actionable.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Refined the cognitive walkthrough prompt to provide clearer, more detailed instructions so walkthroughs produce more consistent step‑by‑step usability observations and actionable next steps.
Reworked the heuristic evaluation prompt structure (getPrompt) to improve clarity and organization, making automated heuristic assessments easier to follow and interpret.
Expanded heuristic evaluation guidance with additional assessment guidelines for design issues, helping the evaluator better judge severity and explain user impact with more specific recommendations.

weeks.label: Week of Mar 17, 2025
weeks.summary: Small maintenance to the Next.js app layout to ensure global styles are imported correctly and to reduce styling regressions. No intentional visual changes expected for users.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Corrected the import path for globals.css in the app layout so global styles load consistently across pages.
Reduced the risk of missing or inconsistent global styles—this lowers the chance of styling regressions while preserving existing visuals.
Cleaned up layout imports to improve code clarity and make future layout or style changes easier for developers to implement.

weeks.label: Week of Feb 24, 2025
weeks.summary: This week’s release cleans up and standardizes import paths and TypeScript configuration across the Next.js app and worker services, and refactors several UI components and backend routes to improve module resolution and developer experience.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Standardized import paths across the Next.js application: pages, layouts, API routes and many components were updated to use consistent module paths to reduce import fragility and prevent build/runtime resolution issues.

Refactored UI component imports and formatting (button, breadcrumb, card, carousel, dialog, dropdown-menu, form, input, label and others) so component exports/imports are consistent and easier to consume.

Updated TypeScript configuration and worker code (ai-worker and db-worker): tsconfig and several server/controller/middleware files were adjusted to improve type resolution and build reliability for background services.

Clarified third-party imports in backend logic: OpenAI-related imports in heuristic evaluation and Prisma/auth handler import paths in API routes were adjusted for clarity and to avoid potential runtime issues.

weeks.label: Week of Feb 17, 2025
weeks.summary: This week’s release improves study lifecycle and failure handling, expands heuristic evaluation results, and adds UI and backend support to better track and retry studies.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Add study retry flow so users can re-run failed or incomplete studies directly from the UI; study status handling was updated so retrying normalizes task types and resumes processing.

Automatically update study status and refund user credits when cognitive walkthroughs or heuristic evaluations fail, ensuring users aren’t charged for failed jobs and failures are reflected in the study state.
Produce richer heuristic-evaluation results: evaluations now include a violated flag, reason, and an array of recommendations (multiple recommendations per issue) for clearer, actionable feedback.
Introduce a StudyButton component in the app to surface study status and actions (start, retry, etc.), improving user control and visibility of study lifecycle directly in the UI.

Backend and schema improvements to track job data and study status more reliably: Study model now stores jobData and a new API endpoint lets the system update study status, enabling better coordination between the UI, queue workers, and database.

weeks.label: Week of Feb 3, 2025
weeks.summary: This week we shipped backend processing for user studies and made several frontend and reliability improvements. Key changes include new cognitive walkthrough and heuristic evaluation flows, credit handling updates, study status tracking, and UI cleanups.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Added cognitive walkthrough and heuristic evaluation processing with new API endpoints and full database integration. Results are now stored for studies and the backend supports file uploads for heuristic evaluations.
Implemented credit management during job processing: credits are updated when study jobs complete and refunded if a job fails. Credit update logic has been integrated across relevant workflows.

Introduced study status tracking (Study.status and StudyStatus enum) and frontend improvements: study result rendering was refactored into a StudyButton component, heuristic evaluation and walkthrough forms were improved, and the interview participate page was removed to streamline study pages.

Improved reliability and diagnostics: better error handling and logging in AI and DB workers, improved validation and version retrieval logic, and robustness fixes for cognitive walkthrough and heuristic evaluation processing.

weeks.label: Week of Jan 27, 2025
weeks.summary: This week we added a backend database service with REST APIs, refactored the frontend to use those APIs, and shipped the first pieces of an asynchronous job pipeline for heuristic evaluations using AWS SQS and a polling worker.

sections.title: Highlights
items: New db-worker service: an Express-based backend with Prisma schema and API routes to manage users and studies. Endpoints include fetching user and study data and deleting studies, with user ID handling implemented.
Frontend data fetching switched to use the new API endpoints and updated pages (studies, interview/participate) to rely on API calls instead of direct DB queries.
Heuristic evaluation UX improvements: the evaluation form now includes data validation and file upload handling, and evaluations are enqueued into a job queue for asynchronous processing.

Asynchronous processing pipeline: AWS SDK/SQS client added to packages and an initial ai-worker SQS message polling implementation shipped, enabling queued evaluation jobs to be processed by background workers.

weeks.label: Week of Jan 20, 2025
weeks.summary: This week we shipped a v2 of heuristic evaluations with new interfaces and server-side handling, fixed form submission so evaluations process correctly, and improved image and recommendation display across the heuristic pages.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Introduce v2 heuristic evaluation interfaces and a new server-side action to accept richer evaluation data and improve validation and processing of submissions.
Fix the heuristic evaluation form submission so it calls the correct action, ensuring evaluations are processed reliably.
Revamped the gallery component for better image handling and styling, resulting in more consistent image display and layout.
Updated the heuristic detail page recommendation rendering and minor layout cleanups to make recommendations clearer and the page easier to read.

weeks.label: Week of Jan 6, 2025
weeks.summary: This week’s release improves layout and navigation across the app, refactors cognitive walkthroughs and the database schema, and cleans up authentication/error pages for a smoother user experience.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Improved responsiveness and visual polish across Studies and New pages: grids were adjusted for better layouts on smaller screens, card layouts and hover states were refined, and header styles were tuned for consistent presentation.

Navigation and sidebar usability improvements: a redesigned/new study page and sidebar refactor streamline access, dropdown menu items now show a pointer cursor, and the More menu redirect was updated to point to the Studies page.
Cognitive walkthroughs refactored to read questions from the database and present results in a results-focused view, improving consistency of walkthrough data in the UI.

Prisma schema and migrations updated: obsolete migration files were removed and the schema was revised to match the cognitive walkthrough changes (database migrations are included and should be applied when deploying).
Authentication and error-handling pages reorganized and cleaned up; legacy Terms and Privacy pages were removed and error pages were updated for clearer handling of auth-related flows.

weeks.label: Week of Dec 30, 2024
weeks.summary: This week’s release adds a new Studies area and navigation updates, delivers a major Cognitive Walkthrough feature and related schema migrations, improves heuristic evaluation pages and forms, and includes a small bug fix and a new UI utility component.

sections.title: Highlights
items: New Studies area and navigation — added a dedicated Studies page to list and manage user studies, updated sidebar links and dropdown menus to surface study options, and adjusted breadcrumbs to point to the Studies section.

Cognitive Walkthrough workflow — shipped a complete Cognitive Walkthrough experience with new data models (steps, questions, issues), schema migrations, creation and review forms, and detailed step rendering so teams can run structured walkthroughs and track issues/questions more precisely.

Heuristic evaluation improvements — moved additional context into the heuristic evaluation page, updated data fetching to include study type context and clearer default titles/alt text, and rolled out an updated heuristic evaluation form for submitting evaluations.
Fixed file handling in heuristic evaluation form — corrected a file reference so uploaded files are now handled and submitted correctly from the heuristic evaluation form.
New UI utility — added an AspectRatio component (based on Radix) to provide consistent sizing for media and embedded content.

weeks.label: Week of Dec 23, 2024
weeks.summary: This week we improved heuristic evaluation workflows: added an optional context field with limits and display, made form/file handling and result formatting more robust, and refined how goals are shown in the UI.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Added an optional Context field to heuristic evaluations — you can now include up to 1000 characters of additional context when submitting an evaluation, and that context is saved and displayed on evaluation pages.
Improved form validation, file processing, and result formatting for heuristic evaluations so attachments are converted and handled more reliably and evaluation submissions are less likely to error.
Updated the heuristic evaluation goal display to prioritize the study name, making goals clearer and easier to scan in lists and on evaluation pages.

weeks.label: Week of Dec 9, 2024
weeks.summary: Small UX improvements to the heuristic evaluation workflow: the user-goal field accepts longer input and the evaluation page and gallery no longer use restrictive scrolling or height limits for a cleaner layout.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Increased the maximum character limit for the user-goal field in the heuristic evaluation form so you can enter longer, more detailed goals.
Removed an unnecessary overflow-scroll on the heuristic evaluation page card to eliminate nested scrollbars and improve reading/interaction.
Removed the max-height restriction from the heuristic evaluation gallery so content can expand naturally without being clipped.

weeks.label: Week of Nov 25, 2024
weeks.summary: This release adds an editable heuristic evaluation title, fixes message and rendering bugs on the heuristic page, and refines UI layout and card styling.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Inline-editable heuristic evaluation title: you can rename a study directly on the heuristic page and the updated name is persisted.
Fixed heuristic page messaging and rendering: violation messages now correctly pluralize based on count, and recommendations are accessed safely to prevent runtime errors when missing.
UI improvements: updated styles for DraggableFileCard and adjusted the heuristic evaluation form layout for improved spacing and alignment.

weeks.label: Week of Nov 18, 2024
weeks.summary: This week improves the heuristic evaluation experience with a new gallery, clearer heuristic type display, and several UI/content polish updates to make evaluations easier and safer.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Gallery integrated into the heuristic evaluation page — view screenshots and artifacts in a browsable carousel/dialog without leaving the evaluation.
Heuristic type conversion and display — inferred heuristic types are now converted and shown on the evaluation page so evaluators can see type labels at a glance.

Improved evaluation page content and edge-case handling — added User Goal and User Flow sections, refined instructions for clarity, the header shows the study name (falls back to “Untitled”), and empty recommendation lists are handled gracefully.
More menu safety styling — the Delete option is now highlighted in red to make the destructive action clearer.

weeks.label: Week of Nov 11, 2024
weeks.summary: This week’s release expands support for additional file and heuristic types (with a database migration), improves the heuristic evaluation UI and form handling, adds file metadata, and refines session-aware layout and copy.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Support for additional file and heuristic types: new enums and lookup logic were added so evaluations can be typed and filtered. A database schema migration is included—please run the migration to pick up the new enums.
Richer file metadata: FileData now includes size and type properties so heuristics and UI can use file size/type information for more accurate evaluations.

Heuristic evaluation UI and form improvements: the evaluation table now displays a recommendation column, and the form submission and action logic were cleaned up with clearer variable names and more robust handling.
Session-aware layout: the root layout now conditionally renders the sidebar based on the user session to improve the authenticated experience.
Copy fixes: wording updated on the sign-in button and the privacy policy agreement for clearer user-facing text.

weeks.label: Week of Nov 4, 2024
weeks.summary: The heuristic evaluation form now collects and validates study names to reduce invalid submissions and make study setup clearer.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Added a Study Name field to the heuristic evaluation form so you can name and identify studies when creating evaluations.
Added validation for the Study Name input to prevent empty or otherwise invalid study names at submission, improving data quality.
Form submission now includes the Study Name so evaluations are submitted with their associated study identifier, reducing follow-up edits.

weeks.label: Week of Oct 28, 2024
weeks.summary: This week’s release improves study/workflow support and navigation, upgrades the database schema and migration, and significantly enhances the heuristic evaluation file upload and loading experience with several UI polish fixes.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Database schema and migration update: schema changes and an updated migration script are included to support the new study model and related data changes. Run the provided migration when upgrading.

Study metadata and navigation: added a study name input with validation in the heuristic evaluation form and updated the Studies page. A new breadcrumb component was added to heuristic pages to make navigation between studies and evaluations clearer.

Improved upload and evaluation UX: revamped file input handling, styled upload button, drag-and-drop file support (DndProvider/DraggableFileCard), and refined image URL handling to include file type. Added a loading state and animations to the evaluate button and form so evaluations show progress feedback.

UI polish and accessibility tweaks: visual fixes for violated heuristic item backgrounds, adjusted SVG sizing and loading animations, and replaced breadcrumb anchors with Next.js Link for more consistent navigation behavior.

weeks.label: Week of Oct 21, 2024
weeks.summary: This week focused on a UI overhaul: a rebuilt sidebar and layout, adoption of a shared component library (shadcn), refreshed heuristic evaluation screens with new actions, and image/performance improvements.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Revamped sidebar and app layout — replaced the old sidebar with a new responsive sidebar component, adjusted trigger margins and menu styling, and updated navigation icons for a cleaner, more consistent navigation experience.

Adopted a shared UI system (shadcn) and new reusable components — introduced standardized buttons, cards, tables, dropdowns, forms, inputs, labels, radio groups, separators, sheets, and skeletons; sign-in/out, forms, and sidebar were refactored to use these components for consistent styling and interactions.

Improved the heuristic evaluation experience — refreshed the evaluation page UI, added a contextual “more” menu with delete functionality (deletion now waits to complete before redirecting), and streamlined action flows with small UX tweaks like a greeting.
Faster image delivery and optimizations — added sharp for image optimization, enabled eager loading where useful, and updated Next.js image settings to improve load performance.

weeks.label: Week of Oct 14, 2024
weeks.summary: This week’s release introduces a new loading pane that sits above the sidebar to improve load-state feedback and smooth visual transitions. The change centralizes loading UI to reduce layout shifts and ensure the indicator stays visible during navigation or content updates.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Adds a loading pane overlay positioned above the sidebar to provide clear feedback while panels and content are loading.
Ensures the loading indicator maintains proper layering over sidebar content so it remains visible during navigation and data fetches.
Isolates loading UI into a dedicated component to reduce layout shifts and smooth transitions when sidebar content updates.

weeks.label: Week of Oct 7, 2024
weeks.summary: This week’s release improves file handling with a drag-and-drop uploader and responsive layout, migrates file storage to AWS S3 with corresponding database updates, and delivers several UI and robustness fixes.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Added a drag-and-drop file uploader with draggable file cards and live display of uploaded files; the heuristic evaluation form now uses responsive grid templates so uploaded items and form controls adapt to container width.

Switched file storage to AWS S3 and updated the database schema/migrations to store file keys (removing base64 image storage). Images/domains are now configurable via an environment variable so served media come from the S3 bucket.

Polished UI and reliability: fixed SVG naming issues, reduced the sidebar close button size, disabled ripple on text buttons, added a font fallback, and added handling for missing keys to prevent runtime errors.

weeks.label: Week of Sep 30, 2024
weeks.summary: The global stylesheet was simplified by removing a forced dark background. This resolves visual inconsistencies and makes theme and component backgrounds behave more predictably.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Removed a forced dark page background so the app no longer overrides component or page backgrounds with a dark backdrop.
Fixed visual glitches where a dark background could show through transparent elements or clash with light-themed pages.
Cleaned up global styles to reduce styling conflicts and make theme overrides and custom CSS more predictable.

weeks.label: Week of Sep 16, 2024
weeks.summary: This week we added a persistent sidebar and integrated sign-out functionality, updated the app layout to use the new navigation, and refreshed branding assets. These changes improve navigation consistency and make signing out available from anywhere in the app.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Added a persistent sidebar navigation component to the app, providing easy access to heuristics and other top-level pages.
Integrated a sign-out user interface and corresponding action so users can log out directly from the sidebar/ app layout.
Updated the application layout and page structure to include the sidebar across heuristic pages, ensuring consistent navigation and page composition.
Added updated logo assets (PNG and SVG) to refresh branding across the app.

weeks.label: Week of Sep 9, 2024
weeks.summary: This week focused on a project-wide formatting and styling cleanup plus small UI/component refinements to improve consistency. No intentional functional changes were introduced.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Updated Prettier configuration and applied consistent code formatting across the repository to improve readability and reduce incidental diffs.
Standardized markup and styling for authentication and loading UI: sign-in, sign-out, and loading components were harmonized for more consistent visuals and states.
Tidied evaluation UI and server route code: evaluate button and heuristic evaluation form were cleaned up and app/api/users/route.ts was simplified — changes are cosmetic and do not alter behavior.
